h1: Eye Care Tips From Our Pine Beach Eye Doctors
lede: Questions about your eyes don’t always wait for your next appointment. Here you’ll find plain-language guidance on children’s vision, everyday comfort, eye health as the years go by and what to do when something suddenly feels wrong. Use it to make sense of a symptom and to decide when it’s time to come in.

sections.heading: Featured Guide for Parents
sections.html:
Pediatric Eye Exams: Beyond School Screenings explains why passing a school screening doesn’t always mean a child sees comfortably, what a complete children’s eye exam checks, and why back-to-school season is a practical time to book.

Signs parents often notice first:

  • Squinting, or closing or covering one eye
  • Frequent eye rubbing
  • Headaches after reading or screen time
  • Sitting very close to screens or holding books near the face
  • Losing their place while reading, or avoiding homework

One sign on its own isn’t cause for alarm, but signs that linger or show up together are a good reason to schedule an exam.

sections.heading: Everyday Habits That Help Your Eyes
sections.html:
• Keep up with exams. Many eye conditions develop slowly and without early symptoms, so a regular exam can catch changes you wouldn’t notice on your own.
  • Give screens a break. Every 20 minutes, look at something about 20 feet away for about 20 seconds, and remember to blink.
  • Wear UV protection outdoors. Sunglasses that block 100% of UVA and UVB help protect your eyes on the water, at the beach and on the road.
  • Protect your eyes for sports and projects. Safety glasses or sports goggles prevent many injuries from yard work, home repairs and ball games.
  • Handle contact lenses with care. Wash your hands first, keep lenses away from water, including tap water and pools, and don’t sleep in them unless your eye doctor has prescribed lenses for overnight wear.
  • Share your health history. Diabetes, high blood pressure and a family history of glaucoma or macular degeneration all affect how closely your eyes should be watched.

sections.heading: Find the Right Next Step for a Symptom
sections.html:
• Dry, burning or gritty eyes that keep coming back: read about dry eye treatment. At Academy Vision, we look beyond quick fixes to find out what’s causing the discomfort.
  • A nearsighted child whose prescription gets stronger every year: ask about myopia management, which uses options designed to slow how quickly nearsightedness progresses.
  • Diabetes, a family history of glaucoma, or vision that seems dimmer or cloudier: our medical eye care page explains how we monitor and manage glaucoma, macular degeneration, diabetic eye disease and cataracts.
  • An eye injury, sudden vision changes, or redness and pain that won’t settle: call us at (732) 978-9306. We offer emergency eye care in Pine Beach whenever possible.
  • Blurry vision, headaches or tired eyes by the end of the day: it may be time for a comprehensive eye exam and an updated prescription.

sections.heading: When It Can’t Wait
sections.html:
Seek emergency care immediately, at the nearest emergency room or by calling 911, for sudden vision loss, a chemical splash in the eye, an object that has penetrated the eye, a curtain or shadow over part of your vision, or flashes of light with a sudden shower of new floaters.

After a chemical splash, start rinsing the eye with clean, lukewarm water right away and keep rinsing for at least 15 minutes while someone calls for help. If something has pierced the eye, don’t rub it or try to pull the object out.

faq.q: How often should I have an eye exam?
faq.a: It depends on your age, your health and your eyes. Many adults do well with an exam every year or two, while school-age children, adults 65 and older, and people with diabetes or a family history of eye disease usually benefit from yearly visits. Your eye doctor will suggest the right schedule for you.

faq.q: Are floaters something to worry about?
faq.a: An occasional floater drifting across your vision is common, especially with age. A sudden shower of new floaters, flashes of light or a shadow over your vision is different: seek emergency care right away.

cta.heading: Still Bothered? Let’s Take a Look
cta.html: If a symptom lingers, keeps coming back or simply worries you, book a visit. We see patients of all ages, and our optometrists take the time to listen, explain what’s going on and help you choose the next step.
